action.intent: Inspect fortress status, population, and supplies before planning the initial development.
Close the status screen and return to the map for terrain and fortress planning.
Designate a downward staircase into the nearby solid hillside to begin an underground fortress.
Confirm a single-tile down-stair designation on the hillside, exit designation mode, and let miners begin work.
Move down one z-level to inspect the newly carved stair and plan the underground fortress.
Open the designation menu on the level beneath the surface stair so an underground stair and initial rooms can be laid out.
Designate a single up/down stair at the cursor to connect the surface stair to this underground level.
Designate a substantial initial underground room beside the stair tile.
Leave designation mode, unpause, and allow the miners to excavate the entrance stair and initial underground room.
Inspect the job list to determine why all seven dwarves remain idle and excavation has not started.
Return to the map to inspect the designated entrance and determine why the miner cannot reach any mining job.
Inspect the terrain at the current cursor to identify whether it is open ground, wall, or an inaccessible designated tile.
Move the Look cursor one tile east onto the rectangular solid region to identify whether it is mineable rock and locate a reachable entrance.
Inspect the eastern rectangle boundary tile to confirm whether it is solid rock and diagnose the unreachable mining designation.
Exit Look mode and inspect the unit list to locate the dwarves and determine the accessible working area.
Zoom to the miner to locate the fortress access and redesignate reachable work.
Close the miner detail view while keeping the camera centered on the expedition, then inspect the main map and available route toward diggable terrain.
Inspect the terrain beneath and around the miner to determine whether the starting party is isolated by water and find a viable access point.
Exit Look mode and open the mining designation cursor, retaining the miner's known accessible surface position as the navigation origin.
Designate a single downward stair near the rocky eastern hillside and let the miners begin excavation.
Inspect the level below the newly dug down stair so underground excavation can be planned.
Descend one z-level to inspect the excavated stair and surrounding stone.
Descend one z-level to inspect the newly exposed underground tile and surrounding layer.
Open the designations menu to confirm the current level and available excavation actions before laying out the first underground rooms.
Move the designation cursor to the known stair location and descend one z-level to verify access to underground terrain.
Designate a down staircase at the current cursor position and allow mining to begin.
Exit designation mode, unpause, and let the miner complete the designated down staircase.
Descend one z-level through the completed surface staircase to inspect the layer below.
Open the designations menu on the underground level to select a staircase designation.
Designate a single up staircase directly beneath the completed surface down staircase, then allow mining time.
Exit designation mode, unpause, and give the miner time to complete the connecting stair.
Move up one z-level to verify the completed stair connection and orient the fortress view.
Return down one z-level to the newly excavated underground stair and inspect the completed digging area.
Move the view down one z-level to inspect the underground fortress layout.
Move one z-level down to inspect the fortress underground.
Move one z-level downward to locate the underground fortress.
Move down one z-level to continue locating the underground fortress layout.
Continue descending through z-levels to locate the existing underground fortress and active work areas.
Descend one z-level to continue locating the developed underground fortress.
Descend one z-level to continue locating the developed underground fortress.
Descend one more z-level to locate the mined and constructed fortress interior.
